answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because nadir only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, crystal is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any voyage approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
